17. Checking and recording a study

David Sarrat González

Source: vignettes/book-17-reproduce.Rmd
book-17-reproduce.Rmd

What you will learn

Save the recipe, its explanation, the codebook, software versions and plan digest, then run the same definition on another connection.

This chapter uses the synthetic questionnaire dataset described in Getting started. You need: the packages and the matching practice connection described in Before you start. Run the sections in order in one R session. All printed results below were computed with dsOMOP and dsOMOPClient 2.10.5. They are teaching data, not clinical findings.

Concept selections refer to the searches and saved definitions in chapter 4, including the separate questionnaire catalogue. Additional body-measurement concepts are found on screen in the formula walkthrough.

Start this chapter

Start a fresh R session in the book-work directory created in Getting started. Run this setup first:

library(dsOMOPClient)
source("tools/book/display.R")
source("tools/book/fixture.R")
practice <- book_fixture(two_sites = TRUE)
conns <- practice$conns
names(conns)
#> [1] "site"  "site2"

The site and site2 connections are ready. Both use the questionnaire dataset; the second catalogue uses a different label for one education answer.

Keep a reproducible study record

Save the recipe and its concept definitions with the software versions used to execute them. Record the chosen vocabulary release and dataset resource as well: a repeatable definition does not guarantee that a database has stayed unchanged.

package_versions <- vapply(c("dsOMOP", "dsOMOPClient", "DSI", "DSLite", "dsBase", "dsBaseClient"),
       function(p) as.character(packageVersion(p)), character(1))
package_versions
#>       dsOMOP dsOMOPClient          DSI       DSLite       dsBase dsBaseClient 
#>     "2.10.5"     "2.10.5"      "1.8.0"      "1.5.0"      "6.3.5"      "6.3.5"

The practice loader records both datasets in a manifest. Readers who chose a custom data directory can set BOOK_PRACTICE_DIR to that directory.

practice_dir <- Sys.getenv("BOOK_PRACTICE_DIR", file.path("..", "practice-data"))
manifest <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path(practice_dir, "manifest.json"))
vapply(manifest, function(x) x$dataset, "")
#>       gibleed       numeric 
#>     "GiBleed" "Synthea27Nj"

Predict the schema, then retain the published codebook

A codebook describes each output component. Before execution it is prospective; after execution it reflects the admitted column contract. Date precision, category representation and renaming can affect several fields at once.

check <- omop_recipe(variables = list(
  age = omop_age_at("death"),
  death_period = omop_date("death", omop_date_spec(precision = "year"))),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"),
  category_spec = omop_category_spec(ordered = TRUE))
prospective <- recipe_codebook(check)
result <- recipe_execute(check, out = c(people = "D_documented"), conns = conns["site"])
published <- recipe_codebook(result)
print(c(before = prospective[[1]]$status, after = published[[1]]$status))
#>        before         after 
#> "prospective"   "published"
knitr::kable(published[[1]]$columns[c("name", "semantic_type", "r_type", "unit",
  "privacy_class", "aggregate_policy", "missing_policy", "completeness")])
name semantic_type r_type unit privacy_class aggregate_policy missing_policy completeness
person_id key character not_applicable 1 Existing endpoint admission and protection; unresolved for unrequested endpoints Ordinary available NA follows the declaration; unavailable and undefined anchors remain NA reconciled
age numeric integer years 2 Existing endpoint admission and protection; unresolved for unrequested endpoints Ordinary available NA follows the declaration; unavailable and undefined anchors remain NA reconciled
death_period category ordered_factor not_applicable 2 Existing endpoint admission and protection; unresolved for unrequested endpoints Ordinary available NA follows the declaration; unavailable and undefined anchors remain NA reconciled

Completed age is numeric; a calendar year presentation is an ordered factor. privacy_class and aggregate_policy describe the admitted column policy. completeness describes metadata resolution, not the percentage of people with nonmissing values. A codebook never replaces a protected aggregate check.

Exercise 1. Save and restore the definition. Does the plan stay equal?

Solution 1

recipe_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")
recipe_save(check, recipe_file)
restored <- recipe_load(recipe_file)
identical(recipe_to_plan(check), recipe_to_plan(restored))
#> [1] TRUE

TRUE means the definition survived the round trip. Keep the published codebook with it so that later analysis can distinguish planned and actual types.

Save the study record

Create a directory for the study definition and its public metadata. The recipe contains the selection and presentation rules; the explanation records their meaning. Keep the actual published codebook, rather than only the prospective one.

record_dir <- "study-record"
dir.create(record_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
recipe_save(check, file.path(record_dir, "recipe.json"))
explanation <- recipe_explain(check)
writeLines(explanation$text, file.path(record_dir, "explanation.txt"))
saveRDS(published, file.path(record_dir, "codebook.rds"))
write.csv(data.frame(package = names(package_versions), version = unname(package_versions)),
  file.path(record_dir, "packages.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
writeLines(explanation$digest, file.path(record_dir, "plan-digest.txt"))
jsonlite::write_json(manifest, file.path(record_dir, "datasets.json"), pretty = TRUE, auto_unbox = TRUE)
list.files(record_dir)
#> [1] "codebook.rds"    "datasets.json"   "explanation.txt" "packages.csv"   
#> [5] "plan-digest.txt" "recipe.json"

The plan digest identifies the normalized definition. Matching digests do not prove matching data: retain the resource and vocabulary information alongside it, and check the second connection’s published codebook.

Run the saved recipe on another connection

Use the second connection from the setup. In a study, substitute the connection to your next participating site without editing the saved recipe.

second_recipe <- recipe_load(file.path(record_dir, "recipe.json"))
second_result <- recipe_execute(second_recipe, out = c(people = "D_repeated"),
  conns = conns["site2"])
second_codebook <- recipe_codebook(second_result)
c(same_definition = identical(recipe_explain(second_recipe)$digest,
    readLines(file.path(record_dir, "plan-digest.txt"))),
  same_columns = identical(published[[1]]$columns$name, second_codebook[[1]]$columns$name))
#> same_definition    same_columns 
#>            TRUE            TRUE
ds.omop.table("D_repeated", "death_period", conns = conns["site2"])
#> D_repeated$death_period
#> 2024 
#>   18

Both checks concern the definition and schema. The protected table confirms the calendar-period categories on this connection; it does not retrieve patient rows.

Strict Circe imports preserve the question

Circe JSON describes an OHDSI cohort. Import translates supported cohort rules into a recipe. An unsupported criterion must not disappear silently. This deliberately invalid example has an unsupported additional criterion:

circe_message <- tryCatch(recipe_import_circe(jsonlite::toJSON(list(
  AdditionalCriteria = list(Type = "ALL", CriteriaList = list(list(unsupported = TRUE)))),
  auto_unbox = TRUE)), error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
cat(circe_message, "\n")
#> unsupported_circe_construct: $.AdditionalCriteria; AdditionalCriteria has no implemented adapter; retain the complete definition. Inspect recipe_circe_check() for all structural issues.

Read the named path in the refusal. Translate the intended rule into supported recipe constructs and verify its population meaning; do not delete a criterion just to make the import succeed. Retain the original JSON for review.

Exercise 2. Can a successful export/import prove that a source cohort used only supported criteria?

Solution 2

is.character(circe_message) && nchar(circe_message) > 0L
#> [1] TRUE

No. The message above is an import refusal, not a usable cohort. Inspect the source criteria and the translated definition before any extraction.

Unsupported settings are refused

Constructors reject settings that have no meaning for the chosen operation. A square-root transform cannot also take an affine multiplier:

setting_message <- tryCatch(omop_number_transform("sqrt", factor = 2),
  error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
cat(setting_message, "\n")
#> number_spec_invalid: Use only the documented fields and required operands.

If the protocol intends both steps, declare an affine transform followed by a square-root transform in a numeric pipeline. Their order changes the result. A category hierarchy also cannot take a distance rule without a separation:

cat(tryCatch(omop_category_rollup("snomed", distance = "max"),
  error = function(e) conditionMessage(e)), "\n")
#> category_spec_invalid: distance requires separation.

These failures happen while constructing the definition, before server data are assigned. They prevent a supplied setting from being quietly ignored.

Exercise 3. Select only the exact people table’s codebook and inspect its category ordering and contrasts. Why is this preferable to guessing from a name?

Solution 3

columns <- recipe_codebook(result, output = "people", component = "people")[[1]]$columns
period <- match("death_period", columns$name)
print(list(ordered = columns$ordered[[period]], contrasts = columns$contrasts[[period]],
  levels = columns$levels[[period]]$labels))
#> $ordered
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $contrasts
#> $contrasts$kind
#> [1] "polynomial"
#> 
#> $contrasts$reference
#> [1] "period:2024"
#> 
#> 
#> $levels
#> [1] "2024"

The metadata records the actual category contract. A column called “year” could instead have been numeric or a Date under a different presentation declaration. For multi-component outputs, select each exact component in the same way.

Recap

Keep the recipe, explanation, plan digest, software and vocabulary versions, and published codebooks. Reload the saved recipe to repeat it on another connection. Read import and constructor refusals as unresolved study decisions. Metadata explains the table’s contract; protected summaries describe its data.
